Representative Jason Crow served in the United States Army's 75th Ranger Regiment. He's now the ranking member of the House Armed Services Subcommittee on Intelligence and Special Operations. In his fourth consecutive term representing Colorado's 6th District, he's looking to return power to the hands of Congress and has found himself at the center of many of America's most controversial. and important congressional matters, an area he's learned to navigate through his previous leadership of the four-country caucus, a bipartisan alliance and military veteran serving in the House of Representatives. Congressman Crowe joined me to share just how he balances the most polarizing issues facing both sides of the aisle, including the investigation into the withdrawal from Afghanistan, the impeachment of President Donald Trump, and the inquiry into the pre-election assassination attempts. We discussed the impact of budget and personnel cuts to special operations. and why it's more important now than ever to invest in our soft capability to prevent the next major conflict. We also covered border security, the use of active duty military and the enforcement of the border, and how countering the cartels and the drug trade are in a new mission for special operations.
